messages:
maria-l: quick heads-up — prepping RBAC tweak for private deploys tomorrow. need a short checklist for keystore/KMS implications. anyone oncall for potential KMS rewrap churn?

alex-k: @maria-l I can be oncall. main question: will the new role names cause our keystore access policy to deny existing service accounts during rollout?

samir: possibly. depends whether we're changing principal ARNs or just adding roles. if we change the principal, keystore IAM policy needs to include the new role ARNs before remove. recommended sequence: 1) add new roles to KMS key policy 2) deploy RBAC change 3) rotate ephemeral creds if needed.

maria-l: perfect. we also need audit-logging verification across the private control plane (onprem). current gap: audit events for keystore decrypts aren't forwarded to splunk for private customers, only hosted.

olivia-s: that's intentional for now but we have a short TTL forwarder we can enable. consequence: enabling will add ~120ms on decrypt path during initial handshake for a cold stream — should be fine for maintenance window.

sec-bot: deploy-gate: canary policy mismatch detected for cluster priv-vpc-3 during RBAC roll. currently 2/3 keystore proxies report old role.

maria-l: noted. @alex-k can you hold the rollout until we confirm proxies have updated keypolicy?

alex-k: pausing rollout now. pulling the keystore proxy logs for priv-vpc-3:

```
2026-03-20T19:01:12Z INFO keystore-proxy: handshake start svc=rbac-agent node=priv-vpc-3
2026-03-20T19:01:12Z WARN keystore-proxy: principal not found in keypolicy: role/redwood-priv-old
2026-03-20T19:01:12Z INFO keystore-proxy: fallback to service-account token
```

samir: that explains it. the proxy still references the old role during HSM handshake. config map update didn't propagate to that node. maybe netpol prevented the rollout.

olivia-s: checking netpol audit — egress to kms-control-plane on port 443 was allowed but tcp forwarding to cert-rotator service was blocked in priv-vpc-3 due to label mismatch. I'll patch the networkpolicy to include label "rbac-rollout: in-progress" for the duration.

maria-l: do we have an incident checklist? if this causes failed decrypts we need to trigger the customer-impact runbook and escalate.

oncall: runbook link: https://go.redwood/infra/runbooks/priv-keystore-failover (open). steps: 1) announce maintenance 2) add keypolicy entries for both old & new principals 3) ensure audit-forwarder enabled 4) monitor decrypt errors > 1% for >5m -> rollback.

alex-k: I'll add temporary keypolicy statement that includes both ARNs and enable audit-forwarder. olivia, please patch netpol. samir, can you verify proxy config distribution & restart one node to test?

samir: restarting node now (priv-vpc-3). will tail proxy logs and check splunk for audit event.

sec-bot: telemetry: decrypt_attempt event forwarded for node priv-vpc-3 id=abc123 latency=132ms success=false reason=principal_missing

maria-l: success=false — good we caught it live. alex, once keypolicy updated re-run handshake test and post the splunk query.

alex-k: keypolicy updated, restart done. test results:

```
# splunk query: index=keystore decrypt_attempt node=priv-vpc-3 | stats count by success
success=true  87
success=false 3
```

alex-k: audit-forwarder shows decrypt_attempt events and the counts above. error rate ~3%. will monitor for 10m then continue rollout.

olivia-s: netpol patch applied, propagation confirmed. no config errors.

maria-l: checklist summary before full rollout: [added dual-keypolicy entries, enabled audit-forwarder, netpol patched for label propagation, proxy config distributed to all nodes]. locking the rollout window to 30m.

oncall: monitoring: set alert alert=priv.keystore.decrypt_error_rate threshold=1% duration=5m notify=#incidents + oncall.

maria-l: thanks team. post-rollout action items: 1) rotate keys to remove old principal within 24h 2) run a simulated tenant-eviction test in staging 3) add permanent netpol exception for the cert-rotator service with a short TTL.

alex-k: creating follow-up ticket: https://go.redwood/issue/SEC-4821. will attach logs and splunk dashboard snapshot.

samir: also filing a vuln-triage note — this mislabeling could be exploited by noisy config rollouts. tagging as medium severity.

maria-l: agreed. closing the thread for now — will update when rotation is complete. :white_check_mark:
